title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act good-cause eviction grounds
requirement: A landlord may evict a residential tenant only for one of the statutory good causes and must serve the required Notice to Quit, from 3 days to 3 years depending on the cause, before filing suit; relocation assistance is required for some causes.
key_value: Notice to Quit 3 days to 3 years by cause; relocation 6× monthly rent
coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rentals: single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile-home-park land, apartment buildings and complexes, rooming and boarding homes; not transient hotel or motel guests; may not apply to owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units.

applicability.per_tenancy: Transient hotel, motel or guest-house guests are excluded unless the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there continually; a unit held in trust for a permanently occupying developmentally disabled immediate family member is excluded.
coverage_quotes: The Anti-Eviction Act applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings, and complexes.
This law may not apply to two - or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units.
It does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant.

exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; hotel, motel or guest-house transient or seasonal guests, unless the occupant has no alternate residence and resides there continually; a unit held in trust for a permanently occupying developmentally disabled immediate family member.
quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent. The landlord is responsible f or paying the tenant’s relocation expenses.

title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act unconscionable rent increase limit
requirement: A rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws and municipal ordinances, including rent control; a tenant may withhold the difference between the old and the increased rent if the increase is unconscionable.
coverage_conditions: Applies to residential tenants covered by the Anti-Eviction Act who are given notice of a rent increase; the increase must satisfy local rent control where it applies.

coverage_quotes: This law may not apply to two - or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units.

exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.
quoted_span: The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
interaction: A rent increase must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including municipal rent control.

title: New Jersey prohibition on self-help evictions and lockouts
requirement: A landlord may not use self-help—lockout, utility shutoff or blocking entry—or remove a tenant without a court judgment; only a court officer may physically evict, and only after a warrant for removal.
coverage_conditions: Applies to dwelling units in New Jersey; entry and removal without a court order are not permitted under any circumstances.

coverage_quotes: “Self-help” eviction is entry into a dwelling unit and removal of tenants without their consent or without a judgment from a court, are  not permitted in New Jersey under any circumstances.

penalty: A landlord who enters without a court order or unlawfully holds a tenant’s belongings may be liable for damages; a court may award possession of the unit, court costs and reasonable attorney fees; the landlord may be charged with disorderly conduct.
quoted_span: A landlord or any other person who enters an apartment or property without a court order authorizing such entry and/or holds a tenant’s belongings unlawfully by force or threat of monies owed may be liable for damages to the tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1).
